title: Storage Design for Stateful Applications
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and key terms of storage design for stateful applications.
Choose and interpret a suitable Docker example connected to storage design for stateful applications.
Predict an expected result and verify it using observable evidence in a controlled environment.

content.intro: This lesson covers Storage Design for Stateful Applications. You will connect the named subtopics from the supplied Docker curriculum to a small, observable example. Work through the visual first, then use the example to form a prediction and check it against the actual behavior.
content.why_it_matters: Choose storage by lifecycle: named volumes are managed by Docker and are suited to persistent container data; bind mounts connect a host path to a container; tmpfs is temporary memory-backed storage on supported platforms. Verify data after replacing a container and practice restoration, not merely backup creation. Learning storage design for stateful applications helps you make deployment behavior explicit and repeatable instead of relying on a command that happened to work on one machine.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Storage Design for Stateful Applications
content_blocks.code:
docker volume create codeleaf-data
docker run --rm --mount source=codeleaf-data,target=/data alpine:3.22 sh -c "echo saved > /data/check.txt && cat /data/check.txt"
docker run --rm --mount source=codeleaf-data,target=/data alpine:3.22 cat /data/check.txt
content_blocks.expected_output: Both runs print the saved value: the file is in the named volume, not only in the first container layer.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run in a disposable local environment; verify the second run before removing the test volume.
content_blocks.reset_steps: After verifying persistence, remove only this test volume with `docker volume rm codeleaf-data` when no container uses it.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming that a successful start means the application is ready.
common_mistakes.why: A container can start while its dependent service is unavailable or the application is failing after startup.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect health/status and logs; add a meaningful health check or retry strategy where appropriate.

common_mistakes.problem: Keeping required data only in the container writable layer.
common_mistakes.why: Replacing the container can discard that layer and its application state.
common_mistakes.fix: Select a named volume or an external storage system, then rehearse a restore.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a command without checking context, target, or permissions.
common_mistakes.why: Docker commands affect the active endpoint and can change host resources or publish services.
common_mistakes.fix: Check `docker context show`, use an isolated lab, make the smallest change, and verify the resulting state.
